title: RupeeBias: Auditing Demographic Bias in Indian Economic Guidance from Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper measures allocative demographic bias in LLM-generated economic guidance (specifically salary estimation, salary increment estimation, counter-offer recommendation, and service pricing) by perturbing prompts with different religious and other demographic identifiers to see if models suggest different financial values for otherwise identical profiles.
findings: The models exhibited noticeable allocative bias based on religious identifiers, but the direction and magnitude of the bias were highly model-specific. For example, Claude Haiku 4.5 showed the widest disparity among religious groups, favoring Jain identifiers while disfavoring Muslim, Christian, and Sikh identifiers, whereas Claude Opus 4.7 showed relatively flat responses across all religions. Additionally, querying the models in Hinglish instead of English altered the demographic ordering and magnitude of these disparities.
